column1: # work-order.registry.tsv — the places the lint FOUND that order or window beads by an idiom of its own (ga-9t9acg.1).
# It is a list of what the lint can see, NOT a proof that nothing else exists: see "What the lint sees" below.
# Checked by `python3 -I scripts/work_order.py lint` (run from work-order.selftest.sh). Read the header of
# work-order.sh first: the rule is priority > type > age, and ONE library implements it.
# Columns, separated by ONE TAB each (five, always):
#   kind   consumer  a site that picks "which bead first" (or windows the pool) by itself. The slice named in
#                    `owner` migrates it to work_order_sort and DELETES the row in the same commit. When the
#                    last consumer row is gone the programme is done (reviewed rows stay).
#          reviewed  a line the idioms catch that does NOT order a bead queue (comments, git refs, one story's
#                    own verdict wisp, a report) — or the DEGRADED-MODE fallback of a consumer that already moved
#                    to work_order_sort: it runs only when the library is missing or cannot tell, so the consumer
#                    keeps its old order with a visible WARN instead of answering "empty". It stays, with the
#          ext       a consumer OUTSIDE this repo (engine, panel). Not scanned; listed so the inventory is whole.
#   regex  Python `re.search` over ONE line of that file, comment lines excluded. It has to match at least one
#          line today: a row that matches nothing is STALE and fails the lint, and so does an idiom line that no
#          row matches (UNREGISTERED). So a slice cannot migrate without deleting its row, and a new ad-hoc
#          sort of a SHAPE THE LINT SEES cannot appear without a row that says why. A row is matched per line,
#          not per site: one regex that matches three identical lines keeps the row alive after two of them go.
#   owner  consumer/ext: the slice's bead id, or UNASSIGNED (found after the inventory, no slice yet — it is
#          reported in ga-9t9acg.1 so the Mayor assigns it). reviewed: `-`.
#   note   R-number from docs/research/ga-3zlzot-ordem-unica/inventario-e-desenho.md and what the site does.
# What the lint sees (the whole claim; `python3 -I scripts/work_order.py lint` prints it on every run, clean or not):
#   SAME-LINE FORMS matched by IDIOMS (scripts/work_order.py) in the files matched by SCOPE_GLOBS:
#     M1 jq sort_by/min_by/max_by on created_at|updated_at|priority   M2 any --sort flag   M3 _PILOT_SORT_JQ
#     M4 Python .sort/sorted/min/max(key=...) on those fields         M5 a positive window: --limit N / --limit=N /
#     "--limit", "N" / `-n N` on a bd query / "-n", "N" in a Python argv list / a $VAR or $(...) size (0 = the
#     whole population, the safe form, is NOT flagged)
#     plus a sort_by/min_by/max_by/.sort/sorted/min/max call left OPEN at the end of a line (its arguments are on
#     the next lines, so the lint cannot tell what it sorts by and asks for a row).
# What the lint does NOT see — "clean" says nothing about these:
#   a sort keyed through a helper or a variable (key=_age, sort_by($k)); a text pipeline (... | sort -k.. | head -1);
#   a window whose flag or size is assembled from pieces or sits on another line than its flag; a hand-rolled
#   min/loop; any file outside SCOPE_GLOBS (docs/, other directories, other repos — the ext rows list the known
#   ones by hand). A reviewer who finds one adds a row, or widens IDIOMS and adds a selftest fixture for the shape.

R5 (ga-9t9acg.5) the wa-worker Step 1b2 probe's FALLBACK: it runs ONLY when work_order_sort is missing or cannot tell, on the pool the probe already fetched whole (--limit 0). It is the order the prompt had before the migration (priority, then age by reclaim, no feature tier), kept so a broken library degrades to the old order with a WARN and never to [] (which a worker reads as "no work" and drains on). git: the newest branch of a repo, not a bead
sling retry: finds the ONE bead this sling just created, by title and creation time (window of 5 is the lookup, not a queue)
sling retry: the newest bead with the sling's own title; not a queue
store liveness probe, the output is thrown away
the NEWEST gate marker of ONE source bead, to read its branch label
one story's own pending verdict wisp (oldest, to be deterministic); not a queue of stories
the comments of ONE bead, newest first
git for-each-ref of remote branches, not beads
docstring example of a forbidden $HOME scan
experiment report: the order of the entities listed, nothing is dispatched from it
portaria shadow: the nudge snapshot, in the order the nudges were created; nudges, not beads
git: the engine repo's branches, not beads
membership set: the source-bead ids that have an open gate marker (_bd_gate_markers). No order is used; the window of 200 means a marker past the 200th is not in the set (a known cap, not a queue)
story:approved reconcile scan: every bead is evaluated on its own and the result is a count, so the order is not used; the window of 200 caps how many are seen per cycle
label scan for wrong-store beads: candidates are collected into a dict by id and each is rehomed on its own; order not used, window of 100 caps one cycle (the rest is picked up as these leave)
diagnostic read (_bd_json): counts/ages of markers and approved stories for the imparavel report; nothing is dispatched from it, order not used
dolt liveness probe (check_dolt): only the exit code and latency are read, the bead is thrown away

ONE reviewer session's own verdict beads (assignee = its session id, window 5): the first non-closed one carrying a gate_run field is read for its verdict timeout; a session holds one live verdict at a time, not a queue
three counters (backlog_signal, delivery_signal, ghost_slot_signal): len() of the open story:approved / ctx:ready / story:in-flight beads per rig, order not used; the window of 100 caps the count
existence check on ONE source bead's own gate markers / runs (window 20): any active one answers yes; order not used
rig NAMES in alphabetical order for a report line; not beads
daemon owner names by RSS, to pick the top N for a rig lookup; processes, not beads
topological layering of orphan beads for cleanup (blocks edges first, id inside a layer for determinism); the order of cleanup, not of which work is served first
the OLDEST non-ephemeral bead of a database, used as the control bead of a before/after snapshot of a compaction; not a work queue
the previous digest bead (newest by created_at), to read its digest.until; a chain of digests, not a queue
prose: the newest bead of one label, to tell "the job stopped" from "a quiet period"; a freshness check, not a queue
prose: same freshness check, monthly label
the witness's OWN current patrol wisp (assignee = this agent): a lookup of one, assuming one wisp per agent; not a queue
the witness's OWN assigned, not yet started patrol wisp: same lookup of one
gh pr list: GitHub pull requests, not beads
